- **Lint:** `cargo fmt --check` passes, and so does `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- **Repo checks:** `cargo jackioh catalog check`, `patches check` and `spec check` all pass. `spec check` printed `2671 rulings, 6519 proofs, … : ok`.

The raw files are byte-identical too: both runs read `commit` from `$GITHUB_SHA`. The two binaries' sha256 differ, so these really are two different builds.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- **Assault-sim's caught-panic error now has more detail.** `play_clean_match` keeps run-sim's text, so assault-sim's "the searches caught N panics" now adds ", the first `<seat>`'s: `<message>`". This was the only difference between the two 22-line copies. It sits on a dev tool's fault path, changes no game, and no test asserts it. I rejected leaving the pair as it was, which would keep the copy only to keep the shorter message.
- **The cards' comment scanner gains catalog's name guard on raw strings.** A name run into a quote (`bar"…"`) now opens a plain string, not a raw one. Rust 2021 and later reserves that spelling, so no card script reads differently; `catalog check` shows the `loc` counts unchanged. `classify` reads TypeScript through this scanner (R2050000), where `bar"…"` is legal, so dropping the guard would have changed what it reads. A new case in `crates/cards/tests/cross/card_metrics.rs` fails without the guard.
- **The two char-literal branches are equivalent.** I checked catalog's `char_literal_length` against the cards' inline branch case by case, escaped literal, plain literal and lone `'`, before deleting it.
- **`conceded_log` has one assert message.** It reads "{conceder:?} concedes on its first turn" for either seat, replacing the two hand-written ones. It is test text only.
- **One new type alias.** `fuzz::NamedRecords<T>` exists because clippy's `type_complexity` lint rejects `read_named_records`'s return type written out in full.

## Worth a second look

- In `play_steps.rs`, `ask_repeat_modes` now builds its prompt with `ask_label` before `run.awaiting` is set; before, it built it after. `ask_label` reads only `run.cast` and `run.replaced`, so the text is the same. `resume_for` still captures `run` after `awaiting` is set, as before.
- In `play_choices.rs`, `play_prices` now computes every price and then drops the banned ones. Before, it skipped them inside the loop. `play_cost` and `why_play_banned` only read `&GameState`, so the order of the calls changes nothing.
